summary: Willard's follow-up clarifications from earlier reels.

blocks.x: I want to correct something here. I mentioned the man who now owns a great deal of Central Avenue and his father apparently owned a great deal of it in his Bluestone; it wasn't, it's Bluestein. I don't believe it heyday. I thought his name was (inaudible) Stein. (Inaudible) Bluestein Property Company Section who runs the Blue Star (inaudible) and owns most of the Second of and Central Avenue, around the Dunbar at this point. Wanted to get that into the record. (Inaudible).

Well, he probably owns quite a bit of the commercial property on Central Avenue itself. Most of the houses on the side streets are still owned by families that have been there for 20, 30, 40, 50 years.
And earlier, in the early tape days, when the Moscow Inn where Eddie South played. you made mention of (inaudible)
Yeah.
I wondered where that was and you in Hollywood. said it was on the Sunset Strip (inaudible).
It's on the Sunset Strip, right. That's what we used to call the Sunset Strip years ago. I don't know
what they call it now. They still call it the Strip, yeah. It's (inaudible) now.
Okay.
It's a lot different now, but --
Yeah.
It's still got the (inaudible) same name. When you were talking about electric bass in Lionel Hampton's band in 1940, you were talking about electric amplifiers, right?
Amplified, yes.
That's what I thought. Wanted to be sure. When we were talking about a Mae West film that you worked in with Duke Ellington, we were talking about "My Old Flame." That was one of the numbers in it.
Yes.
But the name of (inaudible) the film was "Belle of the Night --"
That's correct.
Right.
The two tunes that I found listed in I think Barry Ulanov's book were "My Old Flame" and "Troubled Waters."
That's right, yeah.
